clue.text: Dad's Army cast retaining English illusions

indicators.note: the rearranged letters keep hold of another piece within them
to cast metal is to remould it, so the letters of the sitcom title are reshaped

parts.note: the possessive S counts here as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: The actors of a classic wartime sitcom keep English illusions alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the noun for the actors of Dad's Army, a much-loved British TV comedy about the Home Guard; it is the anagram signal, and 'retaining' places E inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Daydreams are fanciful reveries, a kind of pleasant illusion of the mind.

clue.text: Central heating installed by European poet

indicators.note: something installed by another is fitted inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark

indicators.note: the central letter of a seven-letter word is its fourth

explanation.surface: A European fitter puts in central heating, and turns out to be a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central heating' reads as a home system, but it only gives the middle letter T of 'heating'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine writer of the Divine Comedy is among the most celebrated poets in history.

clue.text: Back from journey before transport appears in capital

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
a van is a vehicle used for transport

explanation.surface: Returning from a trip before the vehicle turns up in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Yerevan is the capital city of Armenia.

clue.text: Up the street wood splits

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'up' means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: fir is a softwood timber

explanation.surface: Further up the road, the timber is cracking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' reverses the whole run ST + FIR, giving RIF then TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rifts are cracks or splits, physical or between people.

clue.text: Real tie breaker for studio

indicators.note: a breaker smashes things up, so these letters are broken and reformed

explanation.surface: A genuine tie-break decider wanted for the studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie breaker' reads as a sporting decider, but 'breaker' is the anagram signal working on REAL TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's workshop, especially in French usage.

clue.text: Church worker heads for chapel and really is taken by devil

indicators.note: being taken by the devil means being held inside him, so the other letters go within

parts.note: Satan is the Devil

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A church employee goes off to chapel and is truly seized by the Devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads for' picks the initials of 'chapel' and 'really', and 'taken by' puts those plus 'is' within the devil's name; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristan is the official in charge of a church's sacristy and its contents.

clue.text: Lawgiver needs a drink

parts.note: Sod's law, the British name for the rule that whatever can go wrong will, is jokingly attributed to a 'Sod'

explanation.surface: A legislator is in need of something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Sod's law is the British version of Murphy's law, so 'Sod' is humorously its giver.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water is a fizzy drink, often a mixer.

clue.text: Pitch invaded by a new dog

indicators.note: a place invaded by others has them inside it

parts.note: a sales pitch is a spiel

explanation.surface: The sports ground is overrun by a newly arrived dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests a football field, but it is a salesman's patter, SPIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The spaniel is a breed of gundog with long drooping ears.

clue.text: 1 down holding container up for young socialite

indicators.note: one piece holds another within it

parts.note: refers to the answer at 1 down, the Italian poet

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'up' means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a tube is a cylindrical container

explanation.surface: The Italian poet, holding a container aloft, is a young lady entering society.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 down' cross-refers to the poet's answer; 'up' turns the container over, as fits a down entry, and 'holding' places it after the poet's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young woman making her first appearance in fashionable society.

clue.text: Ready to take part, young fellows at first interrupting course

indicators.note: letters interrupting a word are placed in its middle

parts.note: an entree is a course of a meal

indicators.note: the first letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Willing to join in, young men break into the middle of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' looks like an adjective meaning prepared, but it is British slang for cash, as in 'the ready': money paid to take part.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge paid for admission to a competition is cash required in order to participate.

clue.text: Cantankerous driver keeps right

indicators.note: the first piece keeps the second inside it

parts.note: a cabby drives a taxi

explanation.surface: A grumpy motorist stays on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby describes someone irritable and bad-tempered.

clue.text: Nancy's first person with second person's servant

parts.note: Nancy is a city in France, and the French first-person pronoun 'I' is je
Eve was the second person created, after Adam, so 'second person's' is Eve's

explanation.surface: Nancy's opening person and the next one's domestic help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first person' and 'second person' sound grammatical; Nancy makes the first French (je) and the second is Eve of Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeeves is the archetypal valet in P. G. Wodehouse's stories, a gentleman's personal servant.

clue.text: What Orlando did in dining room? Starters do this

parts.note: taken as written
the dining room is 'it', the place being spoken of
the setter Orlando refers to himself as I
what one does in a dining room is eat, so 'did' there means ate

explanation.surface: The setter asks what he did in the dining room; starters do this.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'in it I ate': the setter's account of the dining room. Starters, the opening dishes or people who start things, begin a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To start something is to begin or set it going, which is what initiating means.

clue.text: Show off in Venice

indicators.note: something off is not right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Showing off while in Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show off' reads as one phrase, but 'Show' is the definition and 'off' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to display or reveal a feeling or quality.

clue.text: Philistine victory over European first off

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off the word

parts.note: a Bulgarian is a European from Bulgaria

explanation.surface: An uncultured person's triumph over a European, first of all.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulgarian is a coarse, uncultured person, which is what a philistine is.

clue.text: Composing a nice tune, say?

indicators.note: composing means putting together, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Writing a pleasant melody, for instance?
explanation.definitionFit: To enunciate is to pronounce words clearly, to say them.

clue.text: Jolly good luck initially stops betrayal

indicators.note: a letter that stops a word plugs a gap inside it

parts.note: ratting on someone is betraying them

indicators.note: the initial letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Good luck at first halts an act of treachery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rattling good' is a British intensifier meaning very good, as in 'a rattling good yarn'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an old-fashioned British intensifier, rattling means very, so a rattling good thing is jolly good.

clue.text: Dotty, Sue, Pearl, Joy

indicators.note: dotty means crazy, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A list of four women's names: Dotty, Sue, Pearl and Joy.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a list of names; the first is the anagram signal and the last the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure and joy are near synonyms for happiness or delight.

clue.text: A transmitter, we hear, that's collected

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, giving another of the same sound

parts.note: a radio transmitter sits on a mast, so 'a transmitter' is 'a mast'

explanation.surface: A radio transmitter, it is rumoured, has been gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: Amassed means gathered or accumulated in quantity.

clue.text: Missing leader censured dancing bears

indicators.note: dancing letters move about into a new order
the word loses its leading letter

explanation.surface: Without a leader, the censured dancing bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing leader' drops C from 'censured' to give ENSURED, which 'dancing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to tolerate it, which is what one who endures does.

clue.text: Musical item that's less sensitive

definitions.meaning: a song or piece in a show is a ...

explanation.definitionFit: A song in a show is a number, and something more numb has less feeling.

clue.text: Mussels and lychees for starters at The Fat Duck?

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of the words

parts.note: lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A menu question about mussels and lychees as starters at a famous restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fat Duck is a celebrated restaurant in Bray, England; here 'Fat' is LARD and 'Duck' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallard is the common wild duck.

clue.text: Stable provides unsatisfactory cover for weapon

indicators.note: the first piece wraps round the second as a cover

parts.note: bad means unsatisfactory
a lance is a long weapon

explanation.surface: A stable gives poor shelter to a jousting weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable' suggests a horse's home, beside the lance, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stable is steady and evenly poised.

clue.text: After much delay Titan rocket's closer

parts.note: Atlas was one of the Titans of Greek myth

indicators.note: the closer of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Finally the Titan rocket is getting nearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titan' and 'Atlas' are both rocket names, so the surface hides the myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said when something long awaited finally happens.

clue.text: First drops in wood more than adequate

indicators.note: the first letter falls further into the word

parts.note: maple is a hardwood

explanation.surface: The first rain falls in the forest, more than enough.
explanation.walkthrough: MAPLE's first letter drops one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, more than enough.

clue.text: Run-down spot on the outskirts of Derby

parts.note: to spot is to see

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: A shabby place on the edge of Derby, an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy describes something shabby and squalid.

clue.text: The rest of the hussies take part

indicators.note: only part of these words is taken

explanation.surface: The remaining loose women join in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take part' reads as one phrase, but 'take' supplies letters and 'part' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap, a period of rest.

clue.text: Watch parrot?

definitions.meaning: a watch that chimes the time on demand

explanation.definitionFit: A chiming pocket watch is a repeater, and a parrot copies speech.

clue.text: Girl seen dropping odd papers

indicators.note: the odd letters are dropped, keeping the even ones

parts.note: ID is identity papers

explanation.surface: A girl was seen discarding unusual documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional English female forename, as borne by the children's author Blyton, so a girl's name by example.

clue.text: Tea's ready in mess for movable feast

indicators.note: being in a mess means in disorder, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Tea's prepared in the officers' dining hall for a feast day.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter's date varies each year, the classic movable feast of the Christian calendar.
